text:
sqlpipe moves data from Postgres to S3 as Parquet through three decoupled stages connected by bounded queues.

The reader process opens a server-side cursor and streams rows in fixed-size batches, so memory stays flat regardless of table size. Each batch carries its column metadata and a sequence number.

The converter consumes batches, coerces Postgres types to Arrow types, and buffers rows until a row group reaches the configured size. It then encodes the group as Parquet and hands the compressed bytes downstream.

The uploader starts a multipart upload per output object, sends each completed row group as a part, and retries failed parts with exponential backoff. It completes the upload only after every part is acknowledged, and aborts it on unrecoverable failure so no partial objects remain.

Backpressure flows upstream: a slow uploader fills the queue and pauses the reader.
